name: Which National Electrical Code edition each US state enforces: adoption status, effective dates and amendments, from the state boards themselves
description: The NEC edition currently in force in each US state, with the effective date, the adopting authority, whether state amendments apply, and any announced transition to a newer edition. The spread is real and moving: Minnesota's Board of Electricity put the 2026 NEC in force on Aug. 17, 2026 (permits filed before that date still follow the 2023 NEC); Oregon's 2023 Oregon Electrical Specialty Code, based on the 2023 NEC, took effect Oct. 1, 2023 with a published table of amendments, and the 2026 OESC is in adoption; Washington's WAC 296-46B-010 carries the 2023 NEC with the 2026 edition already written in for Dec. 31, 2026; Nebraska has been on the 2023 NEC since Aug. 1, 2024. Answers 'which NEC edition is in effect in my state?', 'which states have adopted the 2026 NEC?', 'does my state amend the NEC or adopt it unamended?', 'when does the new electrical code take effect for permits?'. Caveat: local jurisdictions (AHJs) may enforce a different edition; this asset records statewide adoption only. Which edition is in force changes month to month, which is why every record carries the date its source states and a verbatim quote — a static tracker published two weeks before Minnesota's cutover was wrong two weeks later, and so was an earlier version of this asset.
licence: Sources are US state government pages (public records). We take facts plus short attributed quotes linking back.

records.statute_or_rule: Chapter 1315 of the Minnesota State Building Code
records.source_quote: Board of Electricity has adopted the 2026 National Electrical Code (NEC) with an effective date of Aug. 17, 2026. Therefore: Electrical permits filed before Aug. 17, 2026, must comply with the 2023 NEC. Electrical permits filed on or after Aug. 17, 2026, must comply with the 2026 NEC. Electrical licensing exams will transition to the 2026 NEC beginning Sept. 8, 2026. Chapter 1315 of the Minnesota State Building Code adopts a national standard for the installation of electrical wiring, apparatus and equipment for electric light, heat, power, technology circuits and systems, and alarm and communication systems. Minnesota's electrical code consists of the National Electrical Code as published by the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA).

Beginning August 1st, 2024, the Nebraska State Electrical Division will be adopting the NFPA 70 National Electric Code 2023. At that time all testing through PSI will switch to 2023 code, and specialty license examinations in the office will also switch to 2023 code.

records.source_quote: The 2023 edition of the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70 - 2023) including Annex A, B, C, and subsequent Errata and Tentative Interim Amendments issued by the National Fire Protection Association; the latest published versions of Commercial Building Telecommunications Cabling Standard (ANSI/TIA-568); Commercial Building Standard for Telecommunications Pathway and Spaces (ANSI/TIA-569); Commercial Building Grounding and Bonding Requirements for Telecommunications (ANSI/TIA-607); Residential Telecommunications Cable Standard (ANSI/TIA-570); and the latest published version of the National Electrical Safety Code (NESC excluding Appendixes A and B) are hereby adopted by reference as part of this chapter. Effective December 31, 2026, the 2026 edition of the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70-2026) including Annex A, B, and C is adopted in this chapter by reference and replaces the 2023 edition of the NFPA 70. This chapter will be followed where there is any conflict between this chapter and the above adopted standards.
